limitations: Passing claims are limited to the named Windows source integration, native package, component tests, and existing admitted-module regression checks. Complete WVB 1.39 admission stays closed; no complete candidate execution or cross-host qualification is claimed.

Historical failures are preserved above. Duplicate locals were corrected. The in-module borrowing helper form still triggered an unexplained native analyzer exit 2 even though isolated forms compiled; moving value handling and its shared readers to a focused module removed the trigger. This is not a general compiler-diagnostics repair.

Frame-owned leases retain owners until frame exit, not last use. Repeated exact local/type/projection keys reuse a lease; 64 bindings occupy at most 1792 bytes, 63 saved bases occupy 252 bytes, and 64 operand flags bound state in addition to the 2304-byte view table. This relies on verified frozen direct owners and non-escaping borrowed results.

The new direct scalar cases cover E1 creation/reuse, case and field observations, absence, live and stale view locals, illegal view operands and returns, frame return roots, and descriptor reference retention. They do not exercise borrowed owners during forced aggregate collection, backing-storage lifetime, callable capture lifetime, or complete candidate module execution. Task/provider, unsafe, callable, and owned-payload restrictions remain.

Existing text/bytes, heap-reclamation, and aggregate-ownership fixtures were compiled as small temporary projects, then executed by the final source-built runner with exact result checks and 60-second per-process bounds. The instruction-report oracle was checked against the existing reconstruction fixture hash; its correct count is 4, not the initial diagnostic expectation of 2. No retained verifier entry point was added.

The expanded owner first passed after build/package/execution phases of 28669, 85477, and 1423 ms. Its first summary printed the old count; the corrected 287-group summary was confirmed by the 2483 ms cache-backed run. Final runner package phase timings were 19 seconds for complete verification, 35 for staging, and 53 for container construction. These are warm-bootstrap Windows measurements, not clean-machine, peak-memory, or cross-host performance claims.

The reviewed automatic plan selected 3450 expected seconds and 13800 maximum seconds and was not executed wholesale. The initial approved cold compiler run took 2161372 ms, populated the compiler cache, and failed target analysis. The user subsequently explicitly approved continuing for all time needed; subsequent builds reused the recorded compiler cache. No repeated broad gate was used.

Full memory-budget, independent compiler reconstruction, broad native lowering/ABI, browser, OS, real-consumer, and Linux qualification were deferred because this checkpoint does not claim those contracts. Only the current runner target was rebuilt and packaged; no bootstrap candidate artifact was promoted.
